explanations: There is none. Each of the three goroutines writes to a different field of the Summary (Customer; SLA; RecentMessages and MessagesPartial), and the parent only reads after wg.Wait(), which establishes the happens-before needed, so there is no data race. firstErr is written only inside failOnce.Do and read after Wait. Every goroutine calls wg.Done via defer, the derived context is cancelled via defer so nothing outlives Load, and LoadMany passes i and id as arguments and writes to distinct slice indexes, with the semaphore released in a defer. The optional messages lookup deliberately degrades instead of failing the whole call.

fail() stores the first error and calls cancel(); the other goroutines use ctx, so well-behaved stores stop early, and Load still waits on wg before returning, then returns firstErr. Choice 1 ignores cancellation; choice 3 is wrong since wg.Wait() blocks; choice 4 is wrong because a non-nil error means the Summary is not returned.

The timeout is derived from ctx for that goroutine only; its error does not go through fail(), so it neither cancels the siblings nor becomes firstErr. It sets MessagesPartial and returns. The write happens before wg.Done, hence before Load returns, so no late write occurs.

The select on sem and ctx.Done() lets the loop record ctx.Err() for ids that never started and continue; started goroutines run Load with the cancelled ctx and release the semaphore in a defer, and wg.Wait() waits for them. The semaphore caps parallelism to maxParallelLoad, nothing leaks, and the function does not return before the in-flight loads finish.
